comparator.route: Economic History focus area with minor and internship
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 ESHCC TER Appendix 9 establishes the exact 21-component 180-EC History/IBH pathway; Appendix 6 establishes its historical and social-science inquiry and four focus areas. The English full-time IBH target is distinct from the Dutch-language offering. The public overview contains older first-year labels and descriptions; these do not replace the current formal component names or establish unchanged assignments. Four focus areas are equally specialised; Economic History is first in the current formal table and is the neutral tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Option 1 and its first-listed internship instantiate the third-year choices. Articles 3.5–3.7, 4.3–4.5, 9.2 and A11.2 govern attendance, choices, progression and thesis conditions.

components.name: Historical Identities in a Changing World Order
Philosophy of History in a Globalizing World
History elective
components.note: One 7.5-EC course selected from the programme’s permitted elective options.

components.name: Bachelor Thesis Class — Economic History
components.note: Thesis class in the Economic History focus area. Entry requires completed Year 1 and 45 EC in Years 2–3, including 22.5 EC in the focus area (three courses).

components.name: Bachelor Thesis
components.note: Individually assessed historical research within the selected focus-area thesis class. The class must be completed before submission. A timely submitted thesis has a resit under the TER; the resit grade is capped at 6.0.

components.name: Minor
components.note: One 15-EC minor from the admission matrix, with its admission requirements; participation requires at least third-year enrolment. The selected route does not combine this with the alternative exchange or educational-minor route.

components.name: History internship
components.note: Selected 15-EC field-specific placement, replaceable by two permitted electives. Entry requires all BA1 courses passed. Normally in the second term of Year 3 for History; another term may be requested. Approved placement concludes within six consecutive months and is graded pass/fail.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This option differs from the closest programme by 8 courses (60 EC) per programme. progressionAssessment.rationale: Modern History, economics and sociology begin in Semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses that require it; qualitative methodology precedes later empirical analysis. Modern Sociology precedes advanced social theory. Western Art History in Semester 5 precedes Writing Art’s Histories in Semester 6; the final History Research Seminar examines primary sources on the 1809 Walcheren Expedition. Rhetoric precedes its community-engagement continuation. These advisory sequences supplement, rather than add to, the formal prerequisites and planned offerings.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three concepts survive sequential evidence, comparability, distinctness and feasibility review. The closest response combines direct historical inquiry with economic/social explanation and strengthened historiography. The second changes the governing question to international order and conflict; the third to social experience and cultural evidence. Each retains substantial actual historical subject study and primary-source inquiry; none rests solely on generic complementary courses or a disclaimer. The four formal external focus areas support the candidates; no fourth option is authorised or needed.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both survey modern political, economic and cultural change across a broad chronological and international frame; UCR begins in 1815 rather than 1500.
Both compare societies through global encounters and unequal power; UCR ranges across empires more broadly and is not confined to 1300-1800.
The external modern-societies survey is not reproduced by a separate UCR course; UCR’s broad Modern History course is already shown with Global History.
Both analyse colonialism, identity, belonging and changing historical orders; UCR concentrates on Native American histories.

Partial research relationship: UCR investigates primary sources on the 1809 Walcheren Expedition and writes a substantial paper. The external class prepares a separate thesis in the chosen Economic History focus area.

The UCR History Research Seminar develops historical research at advanced level but is already aligned to the comparator's focus-area thesis class; UCR has no separate introductory Becoming a Historian course.
UCR courses repeatedly connect past and present, but there is no separate historiography-and-contemporary-relevance course matching Rethinking History.
UCR offers philosophy courses, but none of the scheduled courses is a dedicated philosophy-of-history course.
The comparator requires a 15-EC individual History thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.
The comparator component is an open History elective, while UCR elective choice is distributed throughout each 180-EC pathway; no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.
Both teach research design and statistical analysis; the comparator applies those methods specifically to historical data.
Both teach systematic qualitative collection and interpretation; the comparator specialises in historical sources and techniques such as discourse, narrative and oral-history analysis.

Partial skill relationship in academic argument, essay structure and speaking. UCR teaches general rhetoric; the external component is specifically historical writing. No unchanged word-count requirement is assumed from older overview copy.
UCR has public rhetoric and civic formation, but no scheduled course specifically trains the public role of historians.
The comparator's 15-EC minor is an open external-field choice. UCR breadth is distributed across the full liberal-arts curriculum, so no one scheduled course is treated as the minor.
The selected comparator route requires a 15-EC field-specific internship. None of the scheduled UCR courses is an internship or equivalent workplace placement.

Partial relationship in international economic processes and trade. UCR teaches macroeconomic theory and policy; the external course studies economic globalisation and international power historically.
No selected UCR course establishes historical multinational–state relations.
The dedicated historical inquiry into emerging economies and global labour has no adequate selected-course correspondence.
Partial relationship in inequality, institutions and redistribution. UCR uses contemporary economic theory and evidence; the external component investigates capitalism and inequality historically.
Both introduce sociological concepts and theories as tools for understanding societies; the comparator applies them explicitly in historical research.

notes.text: Erasmus provides a continuous History degree, specialist historical methods and philosophy, a chosen focus area, thesis preparation and a required individual History thesis. Each UCR option contains six History courses, including primary-source research, with different economic, political or cultural combinations. UCR does not reproduce the complete specialist sequence, the required thesis or the selected internship. Its economics, law and rhetoric courses are complementary contributions with distinct aims.

audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor History at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies global historical change and uses historical and social-science methods to investigate contemporary questions. Students choose a focus area and complete an individual History thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines historical inquiry with economic and social explanation. The second focuses on international relations, conflict and institutions; the third on social and cultural history. Each includes all six UCR History courses and a primary-source research seminar. Economics, law, rhetoric and other fields support those historical questions while retaining their own methods. Shared rows show partial subject or skill relationships; blank cells preserve substantive gaps.
